IntroducedBillHeader.Sponsors: Senate Committee on Health & Long-Term Care (originally sponsored by Senators Thibaudeau, Deccio, Keiser, Parlette, Kohl-Welles, Benson and McAuliffe)

BillBody.BillTitle: AN ACT Relating to adult family home services; adding a new sectionto chapter 70.128 RCW; and adding a new section to chapter 69.06 RCW.
BillBody.EnactingClause: BE IT ENACTED BY THE LEGISLATURE OF THE STATE OF WASHINGTON:

BegSecNew.BegSecText: A new section is added to chapter 70.128 RCWto read as follows:

BillSection.RCWSLText: (1) The department shall implement, as part of the requiredtraining and continuing education, food safety training and testingintegrated into the curriculum that meets the standards established bythe state board of health pursuant to chapter 69.06 RCW. Individualfood handler permits are not required for persons who begin working inan adult family home after June 30, 2005, and successfully complete thebasic and modifiedbasic caregiver training if they receive informationor training regarding safe food handling practices from the employerbefore providing food handling or service for the adult family homeclients. Documentation that the information or training has beenprovided to the individual must be kept on file by the employer. (2) Licensed adult family home providers or employees who holdindividual food handler permits before June 30, 2005, must maintain p. 1 SSB 5650continuing education of onehalf hour per year to maintain foodhandling and safety training. (3) Licensed adult family home providers or employees who holdindividual food handler permits before June 30, 2005, are not requiredto renew the permit if the continuing education requirement insubsection (2) of this section is met.

BegSecNew.BegSecText: A new section is added to chapter 69.06 RCWto read as follows:

BillSection.RCWSLText: Except for the food safety training standards adopted by the stateboard of health pursuant to RCW 69.06.010, this chapter is notapplicable to persons who work in adult family homes and successfullycomplete training and continuing education as required in section 1 ofthis act.
